candidate_sources.title: Penicillium digitatum (green mould) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Penicillium digitatum is the causal agent of green mould, a primary postharvest disease of citrus fruits. It is a wound pathogen causing a soft, wet rot; datasheet covers symptoms, biology, distribution and management.

candidate_sources.title: Alternative Management Approaches of Citrus Diseases Caused by Penicillium digitatum (Green Mold) and Penicillium italicum (Blue Mold)
candidate_sources.snippet: Initial symptoms include a moist depression on the surface, which expands as white mycelium colonizes the surface; the centre of the mycelial mass turns olive as conidial production begins. Reviews wound infection, disease cycle, fungicides (imazalil, pyrimethanil, thiabendazole) and eco-friendly alternatives.

candidate_sources.title: Citrus storage moulds (197) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens & Weeds
candidate_sources.snippet: Fact sheet on citrus storage moulds including green mould (Penicillium digitatum) and blue mould (Penicillium italicum): wound-entry pathogens producing soft wet rot with white mycelium turning green/olive, plus prevention through careful handling and sanitation.

candidate_sources.snippet: Penicillium digitatum is the primary lemon fungal phytopathogen, causing green mold during the postharvest period; soft wet rot following wound infection. Study evaluates a chitosanâ€“riboflavin bioconjugate for control on lemon fruit.

candidate_sources.title: First Report of Whisker Mold as a Postharvest Disease Caused by Penicillium ulaiense on Citrus (Citrus unshiu) in Korea | Plant Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: Symptoms include a water-soaked, circular lesion and a blue-gray spore mass, with lesions covered by a blue-gray spore mass and coremia with white stalks and mycelia. The fungus forms whisker-like coremia measuring 1-8 mm, distinguishing it from the common blue mold agent Penicillium italicum. Causative agent identified as Penicillium ulaiense via morphology and beta-tubulin gene phylogeny.

candidate_sources.title: First Report of Penicillium ulaiense Causing Postharvest Whisker Mold of Oranges (Citrus sinensis) in Spain | Plant Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: Whisker mold caused by Penicillium ulaiense is a concern during citrus storage in Brazil, Egypt, Japan, Pakistan, and the United States. Identifying features on sporulated soft lesions include grayish blue conidial masses and whisker-like coremia with tall whitish stalks. Wounded fruit reach 100% infection within 2 weeks at 25C and 90-95% relative humidity.

candidate_sources.title: First report of whisker mold, a postharvest disease on citrus caused by Penicillium ulaiense (in Japan) | Journal of General Plant Pathology
candidate_sources.snippet: First report of whisker mold, a postharvest disease on citrus caused by Penicillium ulaiense in Japan. Describes coremia (whisker-like structures) and blue-gray sporulation on stored citrus fruit, with morphological and molecular identification of the pathogen.

candidate_sources.title: Symptoms of whisker mold (a-c) and the causative agent Penicillium ulaiense (d-h)
candidate_sources.snippet: Symptoms of whisker mold (a-c) and the causative agent Penicillium ulaiense (d-h): blue-gray spore mass on lesion surface and whisker-like white coremia on infected citrus fruit.
